title: Symmetric Tree
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (i.e., symmetric around its center).
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 1000, -100 <= Node.val <= 100
hint: Small node count (<= 1000) permits a recursive top-down comparison of left and right subtrees in O(n) time.
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively compares opposite subtrees (left.left with right.right and left.right with right.left) in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal using a queue also checks symmetric node pairs in O(n) time, but requires extra queue space for tree width. Not Two Pointers: Scanning node pointers directly does not handle recursive tree branch comparisons naturally. Not 1D DP: Storing state subproblems is unnecessary for checking structural tree symmetry.
